answer: Randomized grading seats prevent collusion: the engine assigns whose answers you judge, so puppets cannot pair up to trade grades. Back-scratching ripples die when every panel is drawn blind — you wander into a stranger's essay each epoch, and they into yours, never by arrangement. A farm betting on mutual grading finds its members seated apart, grading honest peers, while the tide of outside graders judges its own work cold. Reciprocal fraud requires meeting by chance, again and again, forever. Attacker cost: conspiracy without a meeting place.
